This CS major is for students enrolled in the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). Berkeley emphasizes the science of computer science, which means much more than just computer programming. It includes the theory of computation, the design and analysis of algorithms, the architecture and logic design of computers, programming languages, compilers, operating systems, scientific computation, computer graphics, databases, artificial intelligence, and natural language processing. Our goal is to prepare students both for a possible research career and long-term technical leadership in industry. title: Where do Berkeley course numbers come from? : r/berkeley
description: # Where do Berkeley course numbers come from? Skip to main contentWhere do Berkeley course numbers come from? Image 1 Go to berkeley. I am curious where Berkeley course numbers come from? The lower division courses used to be called 60A, 60B, and 60C, and were part of a series with EE 20 and EE 40. When the lower div CS courses were revised in the late 90s, they added a "1" to all of the CS courses to differentiate them from their predecessors, creating the modern day 61A, 61B, and 61C. When the lower div EE courses were revised some 15 years later, they decided to take the "61" from the CS courses and flip them, creating the "16-series" that you see today as 16A, 16B, and (soon, within the next 10 years) 16C. The two courses meet in the middle in EECS 149/EECS 151 (it was previously listed as EECS 150, I believe). The CS courses are numbered as follows:.

title: A Quick Guide to Upper Division CS Classes at Berkeley | by AWE Berkeley | Medium
description: # A Quick Guide to Upper Division CS Classes at Berkeley. There are so many options for upper division CS classes at Berkeley, and it can definitely be intimidating when first trying to figure out which ones to take. The path people take will differ depending on if there’s something specific they want to study (ie Machine Learning, Systems , or CS Theory). You can always check out other opinions on our Slack or on the EECS 101 Piazza, but at the end of the day, make sure you go with what YOU are interested in, not what someone else tells you to take. ## Upper Division CS Class Options. CS170 is one of the first CS upper-division courses that people recommend that you take. A good class to pair with this is CS 188. Introduction to Database Systems is a solid class to take — it has a manageable workload, fair exams, and is very useful for systems design interviews.
